To study in Australia from Nepal in 2027, you will normally need a suitable academic qualification, accepted English-language results and a Confirmation of Enrolment from a CRICOS-registered provider. You must also arrange Overseas Student Health Cover and meet the Genuine Student requirement where applicable.

Australia's main university intakes begin in February or March and July. Annual tuition commonly falls between AUD 20,000 and AUD 50,000, although specialist courses can cost more.

The Nepalese rupee estimates below use a rounded planning rate of AUD 1 to NPR 108. Nepal Rastra Bank quoted Australian dollar rates at around NPR 108 in late July 2026. Exchange rates change, so recalculate costs before making any financial decisions.

What Has Changed for the 2027 Intake?

The Australian Government has set the 2027 National Planning Level at 295,000 new overseas student commencements, maintaining the same level as 2026.

It is important to understand that the National Planning Level is not a fixed limit on international students. It is a planning framework designed to support the management of international education growth. Students can continue to explore study opportunities, but early preparation is recommended to ensure a smooth application process.

The Australian Government may update international education policies and requirements from time to time. Students should always refer to official government and university sources for the latest information.

Study in Australia from Nepal Requirements

University admission and government requirements involve separate assessments.

A provider considers your academic results, English ability and course suitability. The relevant authorities separately assess required documentation, eligibility criteria, health cover, personal circumstances and genuine reasons for studying.

Students should refer to official government and university sources for the latest requirements and guidance.

Study in Australia After 12th for Nepalese Students

Nepalese students may apply for an Australian bachelor's degree after completing Grade 12, the National Examinations Board qualification, A Levels or another recognised equivalent.

Entry requirements depend on the course. Engineering, computing and health programmes may require specific mathematics or science subjects. Business and humanities courses often accept a wider range of academic backgrounds.

Students who do not qualify for direct undergraduate entry may consider:

  • a foundation programme;
  • a diploma that progresses into a degree;
  • a packaged English and academic course;
  • a vocational pathway.

For example, a Grade 12 management student applying for an advanced engineering course must explain both the academic change and the future benefit. Choosing a course only because someone describes it as a migration pathway may weaken the application.

Requirements for a Master's Degree

A master's programme normally requires a recognised bachelor's degree. Some courses also ask for:

  • a related academic background;
  • professional experience;
  • prerequisite subjects;
  • a portfolio;
  • professional registration.

Applicants with a break in education should provide a clear timeline supported by employment records, training certificates or other evidence. The treatment of an extended academic break varies between providers and courses.

English-Language Requirements

Australian institutions commonly accept IELTS Academic and PTE Academic. Some also accept TOEFL iBT, Cambridge English or other approved tests.

A typical course may ask for an IELTS score around 6.0 to 6.5, but nursing, teaching, law and other regulated subjects can require higher scores. Always check the specific course page. A general university requirement may not apply to every programme.

Total Cost to Study in Australia from Nepal

The total cost to study in Australia from Nepal includes tuition fees, health insurance, living expenses, travel and initial setup costs.

Research degree

Often AUD 45,000 or more

Tuition fees vary by institution, location and discipline. Students should check individual course fees directly with their chosen education provider, as costs can differ significantly between programmes.

Study Application Charges and Related Costs

The cost of applying for study in Australia from Nepal depends on individual circumstances, including application requirements, service charges, and other related expenses.

This may include:

  • tuition deposits;
  • Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC);
  • medical examinations where required;
  • document certification;
  • air travel;
  • additional family-related costs where applicable.

A single-student OSHC policy may cost approximately AUD 700 to AUD 1,000 for 12 months, although the final price depends on the insurer, policy length, and level of cover.

Students can review how health cover for international study works before choosing a suitable provider or policy option.

How Much Money Is Required to Study in Australia from Nepal?

When planning your study budget, consider key expenses such as:

  • travel costs;
  • tuition fees;
  • accommodation and daily living expenses;
  • costs for accompanying family members, where applicable;
  • school-related expenses for accompanying school-age children.

Consider a student whose first-year tuition is AUD 30,000. Adding AUD 29,710 for living costs, AUD 850 for OSHC and AUD 1,500 for travel produces a planning total of roughly AUD 62,060, or about NPR 6.7 million.

This is an example for budgeting purposes, not a fixed requirement. Actual costs may vary depending on the chosen university, course, location, lifestyle, and individual circumstances. Students and families should consider all major education and living expenses when planning for overseas study.

For additional guidance, students should refer to official university fee information, accommodation details, and recognised education resources when preparing their study plans.

How to Choose a Course and University

Start with your academic history, career direction and available budget. University rankings should come later.

Ask:

  • Does the course connect with my previous education or work?
  • Does it include placements, projects or recognised accreditation?
  • Can my family plan for the first year’s education costs?
  • Is the provider and course registered on CRICOS?
  • What support does the institution offer international students?
  • What skills and career opportunities will I gain?

Courses offered to international students in Australia should be listed on the official CRICOS register.

You may also compare publicly funded Australian institutions when assessing tuition, research facilities, course options and study locations.

A mildly surprising point is that the highest-ranked university is not always the strongest choice for an individual applicant. A course at a less famous institution may create a more logical academic and career progression.

Application Process to Study in Australia from Nepal

1. Shortlist Suitable Courses

Compare several realistic programmes based on your grades, English ability, budget and intended career.

2. Prepare Admission Documents

You may need:

  • a valid passport;
  • academic certificates and transcripts;
  • English-language results;
  • a curriculum vitae;
  • employment evidence;
  • references or a portfolio;
  • evidence explaining study gaps.

3. Apply and Review the Offer

Check the course, campus, tuition fees, refund terms and offer conditions carefully.

4. Meet the Conditions

Complete any outstanding English or academic requirements. Then pay the required deposit and arrange OSHC.

5. Receive the Confirmation of Enrolment

The provider issues a CoE after you meet its enrolment requirements and complete the necessary steps to confirm your place. This document confirms your enrolment status with the institution and may be required for official academic or administrative purposes.

6. Prepare Budget and Supporting Documents

This is a real-world detail families sometimes miss. They focus on the final bank balance but provide little evidence showing how the money accumulated.

7. Complete the Genuine Student Questions

Applicants should provide clear and accurate information about their study plans and educational goals.

Applicants should explain:

  • their current personal and academic circumstances;
  • why they selected the course and education provider;
  • how the programme aligns with their future goals;
  • any other relevant information that supports their application.

Each response should be written clearly in English and supported by relevant information where required. Applicants should provide genuine details based on their individual circumstances and refer to official guidance where applicable.

8. Prepare Your Application Documents

Ensure all required application documents are complete, accurate, and submitted according to the relevant requirements. Check official guidance and provide any additional information requested within the specified timeframe.

Do not make financial commitments, such as booking non-refundable travel arrangements, until your plans are confirmed.

Scholarships in Australia for Nepali Students

A scholarship in Australia for Nepali students may come from the Australian Government, a university or an individual faculty.

Australia Awards

Nepalese nationals are eligible for Australia Awards, subject to the country-specific rules.

Applications for study commencing in 2027 opened on 1 February 2026 and closed on 30 April 2026. The 2027 round is therefore closed at the time of this update.

Australia Awards may cover tuition, travel, establishment support, living contributions and OSHC, depending on the award conditions.

University Scholarships

Universities may offer:

  • a percentage reduction in tuition;
  • fixed-value study grants;
  • faculty-specific awards;
  • research scholarships;
  • accommodation support.

For example, the La Trobe High Achiever Scholarship currently lists a 15% to 25% reduction in annual tuition fees for eligible international undergraduate and postgraduate students. The published closing date is 31 December 2026.

Before accepting an award, check whether it:

  • applies to the whole programme or only the first year;
  • requires a minimum academic result;
  • covers your chosen course;
  • can be combined with another scholarship;
  • includes living expenses or OSHC.

Working While Studying

Many international students choose part-time work during their studies to gain experience and support their day-to-day living expenses. Work opportunities and conditions can vary depending on individual circumstances, course requirements, and local regulations.

Think about it this way: balancing work and study effectively is important, as maintaining academic progress and meeting education requirements should remain a priority.

International students receive workplace protection under Australian law. Check pay rates, payslips and employment rights through the Fair Work Ombudsman.

Choosing Where to Live

Sydney and Melbourne offer broad course choices and large employment markets, but rent can be high. Brisbane, Adelaide, Perth, Canberra and Hobart provide different combinations of cost, climate and lifestyle.

Compare the following before choosing a city:

  • rent and accommodation availability;
  • distance from the campus;
  • public transport;
  • local employment;
  • course availability;
  • student support.

A comparison of Australian cities for students can help you estimate expenses beyond tuition.

Common Application Mistakes

Applications often become weaker when students:

  • choose an unrelated course without explanation;
  • submit copied Genuine Student answers;
  • provide inconsistent sponsor documents;
  • leave study gaps unexplained;
  • rely on part-time work to fund tuition;
  • use expired test results;
  • apply too close to the course start date.

A strong application does not contain the greatest number of documents. It contains consistent documents that support the same academic and financial story.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the requirements to study in Australia from Nepal in 2027?

What is the total cost to study in Australia from Nepal?

A realistic first-year planning range is around AUD 54,000 to AUD 85,000, approximately NPR 5.8 million to NPR 9.2 million at the indicative exchange rate used here. The actual amount depends mainly on tuition, city, accommodation and lifestyle.

How should students plan their budget for studying in Australia from Nepal?

Study costs vary depending on tuition fees, location, accommodation choices and lifestyle. Students should prepare a realistic budget covering tuition, living expenses and other study-related costs. Additional amounts apply when family members travel with you.

What are the application charges for studying in Australia from Nepal?

Can I study in Australia after Grade 12 from Nepal?

Yes. Nepalese students may apply for bachelor's degrees, diplomas or foundation programmes after completing Grade 12 or another recognised equivalent. Admission depends on grades, subjects, English ability and the course requirements.

Which intake is best for Nepali students in 2027?

February or March usually offers the largest course selection. July may be better for students who need more time for English testing, financial preparation or final academic results.

Can Nepali students get scholarships in Australia?

Can I work while studying in Australia?

Many international students explore part-time work opportunities while studying in Australia. Work availability and conditions may vary depending on individual circumstances, course requirements, and applicable regulations. Students should refer to official Australian government resources for the latest information.

Is part-time work enough to pay tuition fees?

Usually not. Employment may support some daily expenses, but students should arrange tuition and core living costs before travelling.

Do I need IELTS to study in Australia from Nepal?

Not always. Many institutions accept PTE Academic and other approved English language alternatives. Accepted tests and minimum score requirements depend on the education provider, course requirements, and current English language criteria.

Start Your 2027 Application with a Clear Plan

Studying in Australia from Nepal requires three things to align: the right course, financial planning, and supporting evidence.

Choose a programme that connects with your education and career plan. Calculate the full first-year cost, including tuition fees and living expenses. Then prepare clear and consistent documents that explain your academic goals and how you plan to manage your studies.
